claim: Inhibitory G alpha (GNAI or Gαi) proteins are critical for the polarized morphogenesis of sensory hair cells and for hearing.
source: Inhibitory G alpha (GNAI or Gαi) proteins are critical for the polarized morphogenesis of sensory hair cells and for hearing.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact and is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pertussis toxin can downregulate functionally redundant GNAI1, GNAI2, GNAI3, and GNAO proteins.
source: Pertussis toxin can downregulate functionally redundant GNAI1, GNAI2, GNAI3, and GNAO proteins, but may also induce unrelated defects.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is established knowledge about pertussis toxin function, also referenced in the introduction.

claim: GNAI2 and GNAI3 are similarly polarized at the hair cell apex with their binding partner G protein signaling modulator 2 (GPSM2).
source: GNAI2 and GNAI3 are similarly polarized at the hair cell apex with their binding partner G protein signaling modulator 2 (GPSM2), whereas GNAI1 and GNAO are not detected.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunolabeling data in Figure 4.

claim: GNAI1 and GNAO are not detected at the hair cell apex.
source: GNAI2 and GNAI3 are similarly polarized at the hair cell apex with their binding partner G protein signaling modulator 2 (GPSM2), whereas GNAI1 and GNAO are not detected.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunolabeling data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In Gnai3 mutants, GNAI2 progressively fails to fully occupy the sub-cellular compartments where GNAI3 is missing.
source: In Gnai3 mutants, GNAI2 progressively fails to fully occupy the sub-cellular compartments where GNAI3 is missing.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunolabeling data in Figure 5.

claim: GNAI3 can fully compensate for the loss of GNAI2.
source: In contrast, GNAI3 can fully compensate for the loss of GNAI2 and is essential for hair bundle morphogenesis and auditory function.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3 showing normal hair bundles and ABR thresholds in Gnai2 mutants.

claim: GNAI3 is essential for hair bundle morphogenesis and auditory function.
source: In contrast, GNAI3 can fully compensate for the loss of GNAI2 and is essential for hair bundle morphogenesis and auditory function.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3 showing defective hair bundles and elevated ABR thresholds in Gnai3 mutants.

claim: Simultaneous inactivation of Gnai2 and Gnai3 causes a delay or failure of the basal body to migrate off-center in prospective hair cells.
source: Simultaneous inactivation of Gnai2 and Gnai3 recapitulates for the first time two distinct types of defects only observed so far with pertussis toxin: (1) a delay or failure of the basal body to migrate off-center in prospective hair cells, and (2) a reversal in the orientation of some hair cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by eccentricity measurements in Figure 7.

claim: Simultaneous inactivation of Gnai2 and Gnai3 causes a reversal in the orientation of some hair cell types.
source: Simultaneous inactivation of Gnai2 and Gnai3 recapitulates for the first time two distinct types of defects only observed so far with pertussis toxin: (1) a delay or failure of the basal body to migrate off-center in prospective hair cells, and (2) a reversal in the orientation of some hair cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by orientation measurements in Figure 8.

claim: GNAI proteins are critical for hair cells to break planar symmetry before GNAI2/3 regulate hair bundle morphogenesis with GPSM2.
source: We conclude that GNAI proteins are critical for hair cells to break planar symmetry and to orient properly before GNAI2/3 regulate hair bundle morphogenesis with GPSM2.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by data showing symmetry breaking defects in Gnai2; Gnai3 double mutants (Figure 7).

claim: GNAI proteins are critical for hair cells to orient properly before GNAI2/3 regulate hair bundle morphogenesis with GPSM2.
source: We conclude that GNAI proteins are critical for hair cells to break planar symmetry and to orient properly before GNAI2/3 regulate hair bundle morphogenesis with GPSM2.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by data showing orientation defects in Gnai2; Gnai3 double mutants (Figure 8).

claim: Mouse and human GNAI1 and GNAI3 are most similar in the GNAI group.
source: GNAI/O proteins are close paralogs, with mouse and human GNAI1 and GNAI3 most similar in the GNAI group, and GNAO more divergent compared to all GNAI (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the phylogenetic tree in Figure 1A showing percent amino acid identity.

claim: GNAO is more divergent compared to all GNAI proteins.
source: GNAI/O proteins are close paralogs, with mouse and human GNAI1 and GNAI3 most similar in the GNAI group, and GNAO more divergent compared to all GNAI (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the phylogenetic tree in Figure 1A showing percent amino acid identity.

claim: Hair cell polarization along the epithelial plane starts with the off-center migration of the basal body and its associated primary cilium, the kinocilium.
source: HC polarization along the epithelial plane starts with the off-center migration of the basal body and its associated primary cilium, the kinocilium (Denman-Johnson and Forge, 1999; Mbiene and Sans, 1986; Tilney et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: RGS12 is required for GNAI and GPSM2 to form a polarized complex at the apical membrane on the side of the off-center basal body.
source: At that stage, regulator of G protein signaling 12 (RGS12) is required for GNAI and the G protein signaling modulator 2 (GPSM2) scaffold to form a polarized complex at the apical membrane on the side of the off-center basal body (Akturk et al., 2022; Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: GPSM2-GNAI is a highly conserved protein complex orienting the mitotic spindle during progenitor divisions.
source: GPSM2-GNAI is best known as a highly conserved protein complex orienting the mitotic spindle during progenitor divisions (Du et al., 2001; Schaefer et al., 2001; Schaefer et al., 2000; Woodard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In post-mitotic hair cells, GPSM2-GNAI first excludes microvilli and microvilli-derived stereocilia from the portion of the HC surface where it resides, the expanding bare zone.
source: In post-mitotic HC, GPSM2-GNAI first excludes microvilli and microvilli-derived stereocilia from the portion of the HC surface where it resides, the expanding bare zone (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1B, representing established knowledge from previous work.

claim: Bare zone expansion pushes back the basal body/kinocilium from a more eccentric position near the lateral junction to a less eccentric position at the vertex of the forming hair bundle.
source: Bare zone expansion then pushes back the basal body/kinocilium from a more eccentric position near the lateral junction to a less eccentric position at the vertex of the forming hair bundle.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mechanism of hair cell polarization.

claim: GPSM2-GNAI becomes enriched at the distal tip of row 1 stereocilia abutting the bare zone.
source: Later, GPSM2-GNAI becomes enriched at the distal tip of row 1 stereocilia abutting the bare zone (Tarchini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: GPSM2-GNAI is a module of the elongation complex that also comprises MYO15A, WHRN, and EPS8 in row 1 stereocilia.
source: In these stereocilia, GPSM2-GNAI is a module of the elongation complex that also comprises MYO15A, WHRN, and EPS8 (Mauriac et al., 2017; Tadenev et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: GPSM2-GNAI is required at row 1 tips for boosting enrichment of other elongation complex partners compared to further stereocilia rows.
source: GPSM2-GNAI is required at row 1 tips for boosting enrichment of other elongation complex partners, and presumably actin incorporation, compared to further stereocilia rows.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous work.

claim: GPSM2-GNAI confers row 1 its tallest identity and the hair bundle its asymmetric graded-height morphology.
source: GPSM2-GNAI thus confers row 1 its tallest identity and the hair bundle its asymmetric graded-height morphology.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on established knowledge from previous work.

claim: Pertussis toxin ADP-ribosylates the GNAI subunit and dissociates heterotrimeric Gαiβγ protein complexes from G protein-coupled receptors to inactivate downstream signaling.
source: Pertussis toxin (ptx) has been extensively used as a tool to ADP-ribosylate the GNAI subunit and dissociate heterotrimeric Gαiβγ protein complexes from G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) to inactivate downstream signaling (Locht et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by a citation.

claim: In vivo expression of ptx catalytic subunit (ptx-S1 or ptxA) prevents normal enrichment and polarization of GPSM2-GNAI in developing hair cells.
source: In vivo expression of ptx catalytic subunit (ptx-S1 or ptxA) prevents normal enrichment and polarization of GPSM2-GNAI in developing HC (Tadenev et al., 2019; Tarchini et al., 2013), suggesting that ADP-ribosylation directly or indirectly inhibits GPSM2-GNAI function as well.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ptx provokes immature-looking hair bundles with severely stunted stereocilia, mimicking defects in Gpsm2 mutants and Gnai2; Gnai3 double mutants.
source: Ptx provokes immature-looking hair bundles with severely stunted stereocilia, mimicking defects in Gpsm2 mutants and Gnai2; Gnai3 double mutants (Beer-Hammer et al., 2018; Mauriac et al., 2017; Tadenev et al., 2019; Tarchini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Stereocilia height is more variably reduced in Gnai3 single mutants, with defects more severe at the cochlear base.
source: In contrast, stereocilia height is more variably reduced in Gnai3 single mutants, with defects more severe at the cochlear base (Beer-Hammer et al., 2018; Mauriac et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Hearing loss is more severe at high frequencies in Gnai3 mutants.
source: This can explain why hearing loss is more severe at high frequencies in Gnai3 mutants, but profound at all frequencies in a ptxA model and in mutants lacking GPSM2 or both GNAI2 and GNAI3 (Beer-Hammer et al., 2018; Mauriac et al., 2017; Tarchini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Hearing loss is profound at all frequencies in a ptxA model and in mutants lacking GPSM2 or both GNAI2 and GNAI3.
source: This can explain why hearing loss is more severe at high frequencies in Gnai3 mutants, but profound at all frequencies in a ptxA model and in mutants lacking GPSM2 or both GNAI2 and GNAI3 (Beer-Hammer et al., 2018; Mauriac et al., 2017; Tarchini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A high dose of ptx in cultured explants of the developing cochlea results in a low proportion of symmetrical hair cells with a central kinocilium surrounded by a rounded hair bundle.
source: First, one study reported that a high dose of ptx in cultured explants of the developing cochlea results in a low proportion of symmetrical HC with a central kinocilium surrounded by a rounded hair bundle (Figure 1C; Ezan et al., 2013).

Studies where Gpsm2 (Bhonker et al., 2016; Ezan et al., 2013; Mauriac et al., 2017; Tarchini et al., 2013), Gnai3 (Beer-Hammer et al., 2018; Ezan et al., 2013; Mauriac et al., 2017), or Gnai2; Gnai3 (Beer-Hammer et al., 2018) were inactivated did not report symmetrical HC.
evidence: This is stated as a discrepancy in the literature and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mouse strains expressing ptxA in vivo did not produce symmetrical cochlear hair cells.
source: In addition, mouse strains expressing ptxA in vivo also did not produce symmetrical cochlear HC (Tarchini et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a discrepancy in the literature and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ptx experiments induced striking hair cell misorientation, with outer hair cells in the first and second row (OHC1–2) showing 180° inversion whereas inner hair cells (IHC) and OHC3 were much less affected.
source: Second, ptx experiments induced striking HC misorientation. In the cochlea, misorientation manifested as a 180° inversion of outer HC in the first and second row (OHC1–2) whereas inner HC (IHC) and OHC3 were much less affected (Figure 1C; Ezan et al., 2013; Kindt et al., 2021; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: In the vestibular system, ptxA expression abrogated the line of polarity reversal and the mirror-image hair cell organization characteristic of macular organs.
source: In the vestibular system, ptxA expression abrogated the line of polarity reversal and thus the mirror-image HC organization characteristic of macular organs, the utricle and saccule (Jiang et al., 2017; Kindt et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Normal orientation reversal was lost upon inactivating the transcription factor EMX2 in the maculae.
source: Normal orientation reversal was also lost upon inactivating two endogenous mouse proteins: the transcription factor EMX2 in the maculae (Jiang et al., 2017) and the orphan GPCR GPR156 in cochlear OHC1–2 and in the maculae (Kindt et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Normal orientation reversal was lost upon inactivating the orphan GPCR GPR156 in cochlear OHC1–2 and in the maculae.
source: Normal orientation reversal was also lost upon inactivating two endogenous mouse proteins: the transcription factor EMX2 in the maculae (Jiang et al., 2017) and the orphan GPCR GPR156 in cochlear OHC1–2 and in the maculae (Kindt et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by a citation to previous work.

evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations to previous work.

evidence: This is stated as a discrepancy in the literature and supported by citations to previous work.

source: In single Gnai3 mutants by contrast, some OHC hair bundles appeared truncated, and IHC displayed variably shortened row 1 stereocilia as well as supernumerary stereocilia rows (Figure 2A and B), as previously described (Mauriac et al., 2017).

claim: The same defects observed in single Gnai3 mutants were observed in double Gnai1; Gnai3 mutants and in the LSL-myc:ptxA model.
source: The same defects were observed in double Gnai1; Gnai3 mutants and, as reported previously, in the LSL-myc:ptxA model (Figure 2A and B; Tadenev et al., 2019).

claim: A constitutive or conditional inactivation of Gnao1 did not produce overt apical hair cell defects.
source: A constitutive (Gnao1neo) or conditional (Atoh1-Cre; Gnao1flox) inactivation of Gnao1 did not produce overt apical HC defects (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).

claim: Conditional inactivation of Gnao1 did not enhance defects in the Gnai1; Gnai3 mutant background.
source: Conditional inactivation of Gnao1 also did not enhance defects in the Gnai1; Gnai3 mutant background (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).

source: Remarkably, this unique specimen not only recapitulated stereocilia stunting and extra stereocilia rows observed in the Gnai3neo, Gnai1neo; Gnai3neo, and LSL-myc:ptxA models (Figure 2A and B), but apparently also OHC1–2 misorientation only observed to date in the LSL-myc:ptxA and Gpr156 mutants (Figure 2A; Kindt et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the text and supported by SEM images in Figure 2A.

source: In both Gnai3 and Gnai1; Gnai3 mutants, 49% of hair bundles had wings of more different lengths than the worst OHC outlier in littermate controls.
